root_cause.text: The nilfs2 ioctl handler `nilfs_ioctl_mark_blocks_dirty()` does not validate that the user-supplied block number `bd_oblocknr` is non-zero, allowing a zero value to bypass the dead-block detection logic and cause a lookup failure that triggers a `WARN_ON` when marking a non-existent block.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "A corrupted ioctl request with bd_oblocknr set to 0 causes the comparison to incorrectly match when the lookup returns -ENOENT and sets bd_blocknr to 0, bypassing the dead block check and calling nilfs_bmap_mark() on a non-existent block. This causes nilfs_btree_do_lookup() to return -ENOENT, triggering the WARN_ON(ret == -ENOENT)." The fix adds a check `if (unlikely(!bdescs[i].bd_oblocknr)) return -EINVAL;` to reject such inputs.
